headline: Securing High-Altitude Stays and Wilderness Permits
reservation: Wilderness permits for the Popo Agie are generally self-issue, but organized groups or specific developed sites in Sinks Canyon State Park require advance booking. The International Climbers' Festival in July causes local lodging to fill months ahead. Check the Wyoming State Parks and Shoshone National Forest sites to verify current reservation windows for the summer season.

days.title: Canyon Wonders

stops.name: The Sinks and The Rise
stops.detail: Observe the Popo Agie River disappearing into a limestone cavern and reappearing in a trout-filled pool downstream.

stops.name: Popo Agie Falls Trail
stops.detail: Hike the 3-mile round-trip path for views of the canyon and the cascading water features.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes; the state park is very close to town limits.
days.note: Spring runoff makes the river exceptionally powerful; stay on marked paths.

days.title: The High Country Loop

stops.name: Louis Lake
stops.detail: Walk the perimeter trail or utilize the boat launch at this high-elevation alpine lake.

stops.name: Blue Ridge Overlook
stops.detail: Stop for expansive views of the Wind River Range granite peaks from the scenic loop road.

days.driving: Allow 3–4 hours for the full Loop Road; conditions vary significantly by weather.
days.note: Snow can block high-elevation sections of the Loop Road until late June.

days.title: Lander Heritage and Crags

stops.name: Wild Iris
stops.detail: Visit this world-famous dolomite climbing area to observe experts or enjoy the limestone scenery.

stops.name: Museum of the American West
stops.detail: Explore outdoor exhibits and historic buildings detailing the pioneer and tribal history of the Wind River Basin.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour total; Wild Iris is a 25-mile drive from town.
days.note: Wild Iris sits at high elevation; be prepared for rapid temperature drops.

intel.title: Mud Season Constraints
intel.text: High-altitude trails often remain impassable due to mud and snow until July. Consult the Shoshone National Forest office in town for current trail status.

intel.title: Sinks Canyon Limits
intel.text: Parking at the Rise can be congested during summer weekends. Arrive early to secure a spot near the Visitor Center.

intel.title: Mountain Dead Zones
intel.text: Do not rely on GPS in the Shoshone National Forest; signals drop once you leave the valley. Carry physical maps for the Loop Road.

intel.title: Town-Based Services
intel.text: Lander is the last reliable source for fuel before heading up the Loop Road. There are no service stations in the mountains.

intel.title: Afternoon Storms
intel.text: Summer thunderstorms typically roll in by 2 PM. Plan high-elevation hikes for the morning to avoid lightning risk.

plan.arrival: Fly into Central Wyoming Regional Airport (RIW) in Riverton; drive 40 minutes to Lander for check-in and supplies.
plan.vehicle: A high-clearance SUV is recommended for the unpaved portions of the Loop Road; check rental exclusions.
plan.goldenHour: The red wall of Sinks Canyon glows at sunset; viewpoints near the canyon mouth are best in late autumn.
